svg.title: Parallel SDLC teams: one local VM, one cloud VM
svg.desc: Proposed architecture, not a live deployment. Read from top to bottom. A shared topology describes three logical nodes. A browser observes the control node's scoped projection through its gateway. An authorized operator command is separate. Task actors own gates, teams admit assignments, and fresh role sessions request bounded work. Authenticated peer transport connects the control node to trusted local and cloud execution hosts. Each host binds an executor actor to a VM adapter and runs a check in its assigned guest. The guests do not need runtime networking. Host receipts return to the task actor; diagnostics feed a read-only projection. Transport connectivity is not a check result.

g.text: LIVE VM DEPLOYMENT / PROPOSED AFTER SPRINT 2
Two teams. Two VM locations. One dashboard.
Sprint 2 runs three processes on loopback. This proposed deployment adds VM adapters and guest checks; neither VM runs today.
Actor-Web primitive / API
Proposed demo / Board logic
Trusted execution host / infrastructure
SHARED CONTRACT · DESCRIBES OWNERSHIP; DOES NOT DEPLOY MACHINES
defineActorWebTopology({ nodes, actors, tools })
node() = location · actor() = actor definition · tool() = named port
01 / BROWSER AND OPERATOR
Dashboard · observe both authorized lanes
createActorWebReadModelClient(...)
snapshot(), subscribe(), subscribeEvent(), transportStatus()
Operator controls · explicit actions only
actor.commands(...) → send() / ask()
Separate command admission; opening a view never starts a task.
02 / CONTROL NODE · serveNode(topology, { node: 'control', … })
Gateway: scoped snapshots and events out; authenticated, separately authorized commands in. Not the peer channel.
Task actor · one per task run
Requests assignments, checks receipts.
Only this actor advances or holds a task.
Primitive: defineBehavior().withMachine(...)
Team actor · admit and select
Pin named roles, revisions and grants.
Delivery Lead observes; Tech Lead plans.
Admission is not evidence of execution.
Focused specialist session
Plan → Build → Test → Review; demo
also records Document. One role per session.
system.spawn() · ActorRef.ask() · stop()
Scoped progress projection: joins task decisions, agent/session traces and host observations for the dashboard.
The projection is read-only. Missing telemetry means stale / unknown; it is not a failed check or permission to retry.
03 / CONTROL NODE ↔ EXECUTION HOSTS · MessageTransport · AUTHENTICATED PEERS
Out: assignment + check ID + artifact reference. Back: host observations + receipt reference. Ordinary send is at-most-once.
LANE A / LOCAL EXECUTION HOST
serveNode(...) · local executor actor
Trusted local VM adapter
tools.execute(...) invokes the host-supplied implementation.
Enforces grants, disk reserve, resource limits and cleanup.
Local VM · checkout
Workspace A · Team A · checkout@3 · candidate A
Runs the pinned check on A's input; exports A's report.
LANE B / CLOUD EXECUTION HOST
serveNode(...) · cloud executor actor
Trusted cloud VM adapter
Implements the same tool port on the remote host.
Enforces grants, resource / spend limits and cleanup.
Cloud VM · profile
Workspace B · Team B · profile@1 · candidate B
Runs the same check on B's input; exports B's report.
04 / EVIDENCE AND OBSERVABILITY · THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS
Can I reach the worker?
getPeerStatus(nodeAddress)
Peer freshness, gaps and backpressure.
A heartbeat does not prove guest health.
What did the session report?
Role, attempt, tool requests and outcomes.
Model usage only if actually observed.
A scripted role is not a live model call.
What ran in the VM?
Host: guest ID, CPU, memory, disk, cleanup.
Receipt: image, candidate digest, check exit.
Receipts live outside guest-writable storage.
Join by workspace / task revision → team / session / attempt → executor generation → candidate digest.
A stale guest’s receipt cannot advance its replacement. Unknown settlement holds that lane; never replay blindly.
Trust boundary: guest checks need no runtime-peer access, shared home directory or cloud credentials. VM provisioning is not an Actor-Web API.
